channel.title: The Cypherpunk Handbook - Articles
channel.description: Latest articles and updates from the Cypherpunk Handbook.

item.title: Why I stopped using Linux?
item.description: This article will be dedicated to talking about Systemd/GNU/Linux and the reasons that made me abandon it, at the end I will be talking about alternatives for those who want to do the same.

item.title: Why OpenBSD stands alone
item.description: This article explains why OpenBSD is one of the most secure operating systems in the world, and why Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and Linux are still weaker even when hardened. It also compares OpenBSD with other BSDs, Qubes OS, Fedora Secureblue, and Hardened Gentoo.

item.title: From a strict security perspective, Qubes OS is not reliable
item.description: This article is a critical look at Qubes OS, or "XenOS" as I sometimes call it. I focus on its security weaknesses, note where its design is useful, and suggest improvements and more reliable alternatives for different kinds of users.

item.title: Self-hosting SearXNG on OpenBSD over a Tor onion service
item.description: This guide shows how to self-host SearXNG on OpenBSD and expose it through a Tor onion service while keeping privileges separated and permissions minimal.

item.title: Security terms in operating systems
item.description: This glossary defines security terms you will repeatedly encounter in OS hardening, exploit mitigation, identity control, trusted boot, virtualization, and network defense. Each entry is short, practical, and paired with an example so the concept is easy to apply in real systems.

item.title: The C language's biggest problem: evidence of its insecurity
item.description: C is not a memory-safe language. You can write secure software in C, but flawless memory management is not a realistic expectation, no matter how skilled the programmers are or how many reviews the code receives.
